contract.title: Pressure drop of a laminar flow along a circular pipe
contract.objective: the pressure needed to push a given flow rate through a pipe

equations: mu (1/r) d/dr (r du/dr) = dp/dx   (steady, fully developed, axisymmetric momentum balance)
u(R) = 0 and du/dr(0) = 0   (no-slip at the wall, symmetry on the axis)
dp = 8 mu L Q / (pi R^4)   (Hagen-Poiseuille, the closed form the solver is checked against)
Re = rho u D / mu, laminar when Re < 2300
assumptions: Steady, fully developed, laminar and incompressible flow.
A Newtonian fluid of constant viscosity, in a straight circular pipe of constant section.
The entrance length and the local losses (bends, fittings, a valve) are not part of this study: it prices the straight run only, so a real circuit needs those added.
No roughness: at the Reynolds numbers this study admits, a laminar profile does not feel it.

limitations: Turbulent flow is outside the family: above the Reynolds number this study reports, the answer it gives is the answer to a different problem.
No heat transfer, no compressibility, no non-Newtonian rheology, no transient start-up.
The pipe is a straight line: elbows, tees, valves, and the developing region near the inlet are not priced.
references: Hagen, G. (1839) and Poiseuille, J. L. (1840): the fourth-power law for laminar pipe flow.
White, F. M., Viscous Fluid Flow, ch. 3 (the Hagen-Poiseuille solution and f = 64/Re).

ladder.name: analytic
ladder.label: Hagen-Poiseuille closed form
ladder.method: the exact solution of the steady, fully developed, axisymmetric momentum balance

ladder.name: numerical
ladder.label: finite differences on the radial momentum balance
ladder.method: (1/r) d/dr (r du/dr) = dp/dx discretised on the real radius, wall no-slip and axis symmetry, the profile integrated to the flow rate and the gradient that carries it solved for

ladder.name: convergence
ladder.label: the same solver on two grids
ladder.method: the numerical rung repeated at a coarser and a finer spacing, and the change of the quantity of interest between them

validation: the pressure drop under radial grid refinement
